planting.note: Plant container-grown vines in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with shelter from cold wind, training young growth onto a wall, trellis, or mature tree trunk until the self-clinging aerial roots take hold.

directions: This evergreen, self-clinging vine hails from the cool, wet temperate rainforests of Chile and adjacent Argentina, where it scales tall trees using clinging aerial roots in much the same manner as the more familiar Asian climbing hydrangea. Small, leathery, glossy dark-green leaves clothe the stems year-round, and in late summer dense, rounded clusters of tiny creamy-white flowers appear in a true corymb rather than the lacecap arrangement of its Asian relatives, since this species lacks enlarged sterile bracts. Give it a sheltered, partially shaded wall or mature tree trunk with consistently moist, humus-rich soil, since it is markedly less cold-hardy than the deciduous climbing hydrangea and resents hot, dry exposure. Young plants establish slowly and may take several years to begin climbing vigorously, but a mature specimen rewards patience with dense, fully evergreen coverage that is unusual among cold-climate climbing hydrangea relatives.
